title: Create a Student object
question:
Create a Student class with name and age fields. Construct one student using the sample values and print both fields. Assume age is a non-negative integer.
Subtopic: Class, object, fields, constructor
hints: Identify the data each Student object must store.
Use a constructor to initialize the fields.
Create the object with new, then read its fields.
expectedOutput:
Name: Asha
Age: 19
Edge case: Java's default int value is 0 if age is not explicitly initialized.
explanation: Student is a class blueprint. The constructor assigns the supplied values to the new object's fields using this.name and this.age.
challenge: Try creating two students and printing each one.

title: Rectangle area
question:
Create a Rectangle class with width and height and an area() method. For width 4 and height 3, print the area. Use positive integer dimensions.
Subtopic: Instance fields and methods
hints: Store dimensions in instance fields.
Put the calculation in an instance method.
Call the method through the rectangle object.
expectedOutput:
Area: 12
Edge case: A zero dimension would produce area 0.
explanation: The area method uses the current object's dimensions, so each Rectangle can calculate its own area.
challenge: Add a perimeter() method.

title: Book details
question:
Create a Book class with title and author fields and a display() method. Display the sample book on two lines. Treat titles and authors as non-null strings.
Subtopic: Object state and behavior
hints: Separate stored state from behavior.
Let display() print the object's fields.
Call display() on the newly created object.
expectedOutput:
Title: Clean Code
Author: Robert Martin
explanation: Book holds state in fields and behavior in a method. Creating an object initializes its own title and author.

examples.expected_output:
Title: Clean Code
Author: Robert Martin

challenge: Add publicationYear and display it.

title: Counter object
question:
Create a Counter class starting at zero with an increment() method. Call increment three times and print the count.
Subtopic: Mutable object state
hints: A new int field starts at 0.
Each increment call should update the same field.
Print the field after all calls.
expectedOutput: Count: 3
explanation: All calls operate on the same Counter object, so its state persists between method calls.
challenge: Add a reset() method.

title: Circle circumference
question:
Create a Circle class storing radius and a circumference() method returning 2 * PI * radius. Use radius 2 and print two decimal places.
Subtopic: Methods and object fields
hints: Store radius as a double.
Use Math.PI for pi.
Format the returned value with %.2f.
expectedOutput:
Circumference: 12.57
Edge case: Radius 0 gives circumference 0.00.
explanation: The method reads the radius from this Circle and returns a double. printf rounds the displayed value to two decimal places.
challenge: Add an area() method.

title: Employee annual salary
question:
Create an Employee class with name and monthlySalary. Add annualSalary() that returns twelve times the monthly salary. Use the given sample values.
Subtopic: Constructors and calculations
hints: Initialize both fields through the constructor.
Keep the calculation in a method.
Return the computed amount instead of printing inside the method.
expectedOutput: Ravi annual salary: 300000
explanation: annualSalary() derives a value from stored state. Returning the result makes it reusable by other code.
challenge: Handle a bonus by adding a bonus field.

title: Two independent objects
question:
Create two Lamp objects, each with an on field. Turn on only the first lamp and print both states.
Subtopic: Object identity and independent state
hints: Each call to new creates a separate object.
Change the field through only the first reference.
Print both fields to compare their states.
expectedOutput:
First: true
Second: false
explanation: Instance fields belong to individual objects. Updating first.on does not update second.on.
challenge: Add a toggle() method to each lamp.

title: Use a constructor default
question:
Create a Player class with a name field. Provide a no-argument constructor that sets the name to Guest, then print it.
Subtopic: No-argument constructors and defaults
hints: Define a constructor with no parameters.
Assign a meaningful default value.
Instantiate Player with empty parentheses.
expectedOutput: Player: Guest
explanation: A user-defined no-argument constructor runs when new Player() is evaluated and initializes the field.
challenge: Add a second constructor accepting a custom name.

title: Compare two product prices
question:
Create a Product class with name and price. Compare two products and print the cheaper product's name. Prices are distinct non-negative integers.
Subtopic: Multiple objects and comparisons
hints: Create one object for each product.
Compare their price fields.
Keep the reference to the cheaper object and print its name.
expectedOutput:
Cheaper: Pen
Edge case: If prices are equal, this sample's ternary expression chooses the second product.
explanation: The comparison selects an object reference, not just a price, so its name remains available.
challenge: Change the rule to report both products when prices tie.

title: Method returns a greeting
question:
Create a Greeter class with greet(String name) returning Hello, followed by the name and an exclamation mark. Call it with Mira and print the returned string.
Subtopic: Instance methods and parameters
hints: The method takes one String parameter.
Return a String instead of printing inside greet().
Print the method's returned value in main.
expectedOutput: Hello, Mira!
explanation: The Greeter object provides behavior through greet(). The argument Mira becomes the method parameter name.
challenge: Decide how an empty name should be handled.

title: Bank account deposit and withdrawal
question:
Implement a BankAccount with private balance, deposit(amount), and withdraw(amount). Reject non-positive deposits, negative withdrawals, and withdrawals larger than the balance. Start with 1000, deposit 250, then withdraw 400. Print the final balance.
Subtopic: Encapsulation and state transitions
hints: Keep balance private so callers cannot change it directly.
Validate each transaction before modifying balance.
Expose the balance through a getter.
expectedOutput:
Balance: 850
Edge case: Invalid transactions leave the balance unchanged.
explanation: deposit and withdraw return success/failure and update state only after validation. The getter provides controlled read access.
challenge: Add a transaction history list.

title: Student average and grade
question:
Create a StudentResult class storing three marks from 0 to 100. Provide average() and grade(): A for average >= 80, B for >= 60, C for >= 40, otherwise F. Use marks 80, 70, and 90.
Subtopic: Object methods and conditional logic
hints: Validate marks when the object is created.
Use 3.0 to avoid integer division.
Check grade thresholds from highest to lowest.
expectedOutput:
Average: 80.00
Grade: A
Edge case: Any mark outside 0–100 causes IllegalArgumentException.
explanation: The constructor enforces valid state. average() computes a floating-point mean, and grade() classifies that mean.
challenge: Support any number of marks using an int array.

title: Track inventory stock
question:
Create an InventoryItem with a private stock count. restock(quantity) accepts only positive values; sell(quantity) succeeds only when quantity is positive and available. Start at 8, sell 3, restock 5, then print stock.
Subtopic: Encapsulation and guarded updates
hints: Keep stock private.
Check quantity before changing stock.
Use the return value to indicate whether an operation succeeded.
expectedOutput:
Stock: 10
Edge case: Selling more than available stock is rejected.
explanation: Each operation preserves the invariant stock >= 0 by rejecting invalid sales and restocks.
challenge: Add a low-stock warning when stock falls below 3.

title: Overloaded constructors
question:
Create a Point class with x and y. Provide Point(x, y) and Point(value), where the one-argument constructor creates (value, value). Print a point created with 5.
Subtopic: Constructor overloading and this()
hints: Constructors can share a name but differ in parameter lists.
Use this(x, y) as the first statement to delegate.
Override toString() for readable output.
explanation: The single-argument constructor delegates to the two-argument constructor, keeping initialization logic in one place.
challenge: Add a no-argument constructor that creates (0, 0).

title: Class-level object counter
question:
Create a Ticket class that counts how many Ticket objects have been constructed. Create three objects and print the count. The count belongs to the class, not each ticket.
Subtopic: Static fields versus instance fields
hints: A static field is shared by all instances.
Increment the shared field inside the constructor.
Read it using the class name.
expectedOutput: Tickets created: 3
explanation: The constructor runs once per object. Since created is static, each constructor call updates the same counter.
challenge: Track active tickets separately from total created.

title: Immutable temperature reading
question:
Create an immutable Temperature class storing Celsius in a private final double. Provide a getter and fahrenheit() conversion. For 25°C, print Celsius and Fahrenheit to one decimal place.
Subtopic: Final fields and immutability
hints: Mark the field private and final.
Do not provide a setter.
Use the conversion formula with floating-point arithmetic.
explanation: After construction, the final field cannot be reassigned. A getter exposes the value without allowing mutation.
challenge: Reject non-finite temperature inputs using Double.isFinite.

title: Transfer between accounts
question:
Implement transferTo(other, amount) for a BankAccount with private balance. A transfer succeeds only for a positive amount, enough source funds, and a non-null destination. Transfer 300 from an account with 900 to one with 100, then print both balances.
Subtopic: Object interaction and invariants
hints: The method must interact with two objects.
Validate every failure condition before changing either balance.
Update both accounts only after validation succeeds.
expectedOutput:
Success: true
Source: 600
Destination: 400
Edge case: Null, self-transfer, non-positive amounts, and insufficient funds are rejected.
explanation: Validation happens before mutation, so rejected transfers leave both balances unchanged. The self-transfer guard avoids unnecessary changes.
challenge: Return a result object with a failure reason.

title: Compare objects by value
question:
Create a Coordinate class with x and y and override equals(Object) so coordinates with equal values compare equal. Compare (2, 4) with a separate (2, 4) and print the result. Use instanceof safely.
Subtopic: equals and value equality
hints: Reference equality and value equality are different.
Handle identical references first.
Check the object's type before casting and compare both fields.
expectedOutput:
Same values: true
Edge case: equals(null) returns false.
explanation: Two distinct objects can represent the same value. The override compares coordinates rather than memory identity.
challenge: Override hashCode() consistently and use coordinates as HashMap keys.

title: Method overloading for a calculator
question:
Create a Calculator class with add(int, int) and add(double, double). Call both methods and print their results. Use 3 and 4, then 1.5 and 2.25.
Subtopic: Method overloading
hints: Overloaded methods share a name but have different parameter types or counts.
The compiler chooses an overload based on argument types.
Use printf to control decimal formatting.
explanation: Both methods are named add, but their parameter signatures differ. Java selects the matching overload at compile time.
challenge: Add an overload that accepts three integers.

title: Defensive copy of a list
question:
Create a Playlist class that stores a list of song names. Copy the incoming list in the constructor and return a copy from getSongs(). Modify the original list and the returned list; the playlist must remain unchanged.
Subtopic: References, aliasing, and defensive copying
hints: A list field stores a reference to a mutable object.
Copy the list when receiving it.
Also return a copy so callers cannot mutate internal state.
expectedOutput: [Intro, Finale]
explanation: Without copies, the caller and Playlist could share the same mutable list. Defensive copies protect the object's internal state.
challenge: Use List.copyOf for an unmodifiable snapshot.

title: Polymorphic payment methods
question:
Create a Payment base class with pay() and two subclasses CardPayment and CashPayment that override it. Store both as Payment references and call pay() in a loop. Print each payment's message.
Subtopic: Inheritance, overriding, and dynamic dispatch
hints: Declare a common superclass with a method.
Override the method in each subclass.
Call through superclass references and observe runtime dispatch.
expectedOutput:
Paid by card
Paid by cash
explanation: Although the array type is Payment[], Java invokes the overridden method of each actual object at runtime.

examples.expected_output:
Paid by card
Paid by cash

challenge: Add UpiPayment without changing the loop.

title: Sort employees by salary
question:
Create Employee objects with names and salaries. Sort them by ascending salary, breaking ties alphabetically by name. Print name and salary. Use the sample employees: Zed 50000, Ana 40000, Bo 40000.
Subtopic: Objects, Comparator, and sorting
hints: Store employees as objects in a list.
Sort by salary first, then add a secondary comparator for name.
Print after sorting to make the order visible.
explanation: The comparator defines a deterministic ordering. The secondary name comparison handles equal salaries.
challenge: Sort descending by salary while keeping alphabetical tie-breaking.

title: Detect overlapping rectangles
question:
Create a Rectangle class represented by left, bottom, width, and height. Implement overlaps(other) for positive dimensions; rectangles that only touch at an edge are not overlapping. Test rectangles (0,0,4,3) and (3,1,2,2).
Subtopic: Composition, methods, and geometric reasoning
hints: Represent each rectangle with its lower-left point and dimensions.
Two rectangles overlap only if their projections overlap on both axes.
Use strict inequalities so edge-touching alone is not overlap.
expectedOutput:
Overlap: true
Edge case: Rectangles that only share an edge return false.
explanation: The method checks horizontal and vertical intersection. All four strict comparisons must hold for positive-area overlap.
challenge: Add a test for rectangles with negative coordinates.

title: Find the most expensive product
question:
Create Product objects and find the most expensive one. If prices tie, choose the lexicographically smallest name. If the list is empty, print No products. Use the sample list Laptop 60000, Mouse 800, Monitor 12000, Tablet 60000.
Subtopic: Collections and object-based aggregation
hints: Track the best object seen so far.
Replace it for a higher price.
For equal prices, compare names; initialize best to null for an empty list.
expectedOutput:
Laptop: 60000
Edge case: An empty product list prints No products.
explanation: The single pass takes O(n) time. The tie-breaking condition makes the result deterministic.
challenge: Return the top three products without sorting the entire list.

title: Validate and normalize a user profile
question:
Create a UserProfile class that trims a username and stores it in lowercase using Locale.ROOT. Reject null or blank names with IllegalArgumentException. Create a profile from '  AkShAt  ' and print the normalized username.
Subtopic: Encapsulation, validation, and normalization
hints: Validate before calling methods on the input.
Trim surrounding whitespace, then normalize case.
Use Locale.ROOT for locale-independent identifier normalization.
expectedOutput:
akshat
Edge case: null, empty, or whitespace-only names are rejected.
explanation: The constructor enforces a clean, immutable username. Locale.ROOT avoids language-specific casing behavior for identifiers.
challenge: Add a length constraint of 3 to 20 characters.

title: Merge two time intervals
question:
Create an Interval class with start and end, where start <= end. Given two intervals, merge them if they overlap or touch; otherwise print them separately in start order. Test [1,5] and [5,8].
Subtopic: Value objects and interval algorithms
hints: Treat intervals as objects with start and end values.
Intervals merge if neither one ends strictly before the other starts.
When disjoint, output them in ascending start order.
expectedOutput:
[1,8]
Edge case: Touching endpoints merge in this problem.
explanation: The strict disjointness check makes [1,5] and [5,8] merge. For disjoint intervals, the conditional orders them by start.
challenge: Extend the solution to merge a list of intervals efficiently.

title: Model a shopping cart total
question:
Create Product and CartItem classes. A CartItem holds a Product and quantity; its subtotal is price times quantity. Sum the subtotals for two items and print the total. Reject non-positive quantities and negative prices.
Subtopic: Composition and aggregation
hints: A CartItem has a Product, which is composition/has-a modeling.
Calculate each line total in CartItem.subtotal().
Use long for multiplication and accumulation to reduce overflow risk.
expectedOutput:
Total: 1060
Edge case: Invalid prices or quantities are rejected during construction.
explanation: Each class owns one responsibility: Product stores product data, CartItem computes a line subtotal, and main aggregates all subtotals.
challenge: Add a discount percentage to each CartItem.

title: Cache an expensive calculation per object
question:
Create a Report class whose wordCount() lazily computes and caches the number of whitespace-separated words in its text. Repeated calls should return the same cached result. Treat null or blank text as zero words.
Subtopic: Lazy initialization and object state
hints: Use a nullable wrapper to represent 'not calculated yet'.
Normalize null and whitespace-only text before splitting.
Only calculate when the cache is empty, then reuse the result.
expectedOutput:
5
5
Edge case: null or blank text returns 0.
explanation: The cached Integer distinguishes an uncomputed value from a computed count of zero. The second call reuses the stored result.
challenge: Discuss thread safety if multiple threads call wordCount() concurrently.

title: Implement equality and hashing for an entity key
question:
Create an EmployeeKey identified by department and employeeId. Override equals and hashCode consistently, then put one key in a HashSet and test membership using a separate equal key.
Subtopic: equals/hashCode contract and hash collections
hints: Define which fields determine identity.
equals and hashCode must use the same identity fields.
HashSet membership uses hashing and then equality checks.
expectedOutput:
true
false
Edge case: A null department is rejected by the constructor.
explanation: Hash-based collections rely on equal objects having equal hash codes. The immutable identity fields keep the key stable while stored in the set.
challenge: Add a test proving duplicate keys do not increase the set size.

title: Choose the best delivery option
question:
Define a DeliveryOption interface with cost() and name(). Implement StandardDelivery and ExpressDelivery. Given a maximum budget, select the cheapest option within budget; break equal-cost ties by name. For budget 100, Standard costs 60 and Express costs 100.
Subtopic: Interfaces, polymorphism, and selection logic
hints: Program against the DeliveryOption interface, not concrete class types.
Ignore options that exceed the budget.
Choose lower cost first, then compare names for ties.
expectedOutput:
Standard: 60
Edge case: If no option fits the budget, print No option within budget.
explanation: The loop works with any implementation of the interface. Its selection condition applies budget filtering and deterministic tie-breaking in one pass.
challenge: Add delivery time as a second criterion after cost.
